headline: Majors hold technical structure while momentum fades; big money quietly moving coins onto exchanges as the crowd stays greedy.
paragraphs: All seven major assets sit above their 200-day simple moving averages, and Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all have golden crosses in place, signaling the long-term trend remains constructive. That structure has not broken. However, every asset is down on the day: Bitcoin down 2.8%, Ethereum down 4.0%, Solana down 3.3%. The weakness is more pronounced over the week (Bitcoin down 4.8%, BNB down 6.4%, Doge down 8.9%), yet the month-to-date picture inverts sharply, Bitcoin up 19.7%, Ethereum up 29.9%, Solana up 34.9%. This window disagreement is the defining characteristic of today's tape: a strong rally that has not rolled over, a pullback that has not yet violated the rails. The technical regime is intact; the momentum within it is cooling.

Momentum indicators confirm the rest. Across all majors, RSI-14 sits between 46.5 and 55.2, and MACD is below signal on every single asset. No asset is overbought, and no asset is accelerating. This is not a collapse, it is a pause. Bitcoin and Ethereum hover right at neutral (RSI 49.4 and 51.5 respectively), while Doge and ADA sit a touch lower (46.5 and 47.4). Volatility remains elevated: Bitcoin at 49.0% annualized, Ethereum at 73.3%, Solana at 68.2%, and XRP at an extreme 91.0%. The range over the 90-day window has been large for every asset. Distance from 12-month highs is substantial across the board, Bitcoin at 39.1% below its high, Ethereum 48.6%, Solana 60%, Doge 71.1%, ADA 78.2%, which means there is room above but also a reminder that these assets have traveled far from where they peaked.

Derivatives positioning shows crowding with lopsided exposure. Bitcoin funding is expensive (0.92% per eight hours, annualizing to 10.1%), and the long-to-short ratio stands at 1.71, meaning for every short there are 1.71 longs paying that premium. Ethereum has flipped: funding is flat (negative 0.04%), but the long-short ratio is even more skewed at 2.04. Solana has gone negative on funding (negative 0.5%, annualizing to negative 5.4%), the only major where shorts are being paid, yet the ratio is 2.2 longs to every short. Doge stands at 4.75 longs per short, the most extreme ratio in the set, on light funding (0.15% per eight hours). In the last hour, liquidations have been asymmetric: Bitcoin saw $1.68 million in long liquidations against only $75,823 in short liquidations; Ethereum saw the reverse, $39,956 longs against $778,376 shorts, a 20-to-1 swing favoring bears. The positioning is crowded, the cost to hold longs is mixed (expensive in Bitcoin, cheap in Ethereum and Solana), and today's liquidations suggest some long positions are being tested, at least in Ethereum.

Whale activity reveals an orderly move onto exchanges. Over the last 24 hours, net $174.2 million moved onto exchanges, led by Bitcoin $76.9 million into Binance and Ethereum $125.9 million into Coinbase Institutional (split across two deposits of $73.8 million and $52.2 million). This pattern repeats weekly: week ending August 25 saw $1.056 billion move onto exchanges, September 8 saw $225 million, and the week ending September 15 brought another $739 million onto exchanges. Only CRO moved off-exchange ($28.7 million out of Crypto.com), a minor counterflow. ETF net flows are fragmented: Bitcoin ETFs saw inflow of $159.9 million on September 14, but the last five sessions posted outflow of $302.8 million, showing only one same-direction day; Ethereum ETFs were steadier, inflow of $121.1 million on the 14th and $318 million over five sessions, with two same-direction days. Stablecoins grew 1.35% over 30 days to $310.3 billion, maintaining dry powder. The big picture is whales adding coins to exchange inventory while traditional finance flows are mixed on Bitcoin and positive on Ethereum.

Sentiment stands at 69 (Greed) with a 30-day range of 31 to 74, placing the crowd near the upper end but not extreme. The Fear & Greed gauge does not match the positioning tape: the market is not panicking (no extreme fear) but neither is it euphoric, yet derivative positioning remains crowded and expensive in Bitcoin, and whale accumulation onto exchanges is persistent and material. This disagreement, calm sentiment paired with heavy exchange inflows and high leverage, typically precedes either a test of resistance or a flush of weak longs. The technical structure remains above the 200-day, but the weekly losses, the funding divergence between Bitcoin (expensive) and Ethereum (flat), and the asymmetric liquidations today (longs in Bitcoin, shorts in Ethereum) suggest the tape is sorting itself.

Watch for three things: first, whether Bitcoin can hold above its 200-day moving average if prices test lower (currently above, but 4.8% down on the week leaves little margin); second, whether Ethereum's negative funding persists and the long-short ratio begins to compress from 2.04 (current crowding is a tell); third, whether the weekly flow pattern reverses, i.e., coins moving back off exchanges and into cold storage. Until one of those conditions flips, the regime holds on the daily chart, but the momentum is not accelerating and the positioning is vulnerable to a test.
